shape_note: SD-20 fixture-shape decision, documented identically across all six Epic 2-7 wire-fixture parity fixtures (spellbook_parity.json, feat_prereqs_parity.json, skill_allocation_parity.json, equipment_effects_parity.json, damage_total_parity.json, level_up_parity.json): technical-design.md section 1.2 illustrates a CharacterInput -> PilotReceipt shaped fixture, but Epic 8's own integration-closure cycle (tests/sd20_tabletop_readiness_integration.rs module doc comment, Finding 1) found Epics 2-7's compute functions are never wired into PilotReceipt / printed_sheet_cell_map at all -- each epic's real seam takes and returns its own distinct type, not a CharacterInput/PilotReceipt pair. Section 1.2's illustrative format therefore does not fit Epics 2-7 as actually landed. This fixture instead captures that epic's OWN real compute function's input -> output round trip directly: {name, epic, seam_function, input, expected_output}, where input/expected_output mirror the real Rust input/output types field-by-field. A Rust enum variant is represented as its Debug-format string; a Rust Option::None is represented as JSON null. Only boundary_contract_parity.json (Epic 1) and human_fighter_level_1_tabletop.json (Epic 8) are genuinely CharacterInput -> PilotReceipt shaped, because only Epic 1's contract and Epic 8's integration test actually route through that pipeline.
